evidence_quotes.quote: This article is aimed at contributing to the reflection and debate on the water and sanitation policies in Argentina. For this purpose, regulatory and institutional aspects are discussed regarding services management in the country.

El presente artículo tiene como propósito central contribuir al debate y a la reflexión sobre el devenir de la política de agua y saneamiento en Argentina, a partir de presentar una periodización de cada una de las etapas, que permita contextualizar los desafíos que enfrenta el sector transcurrido una década y media del siglo XXI.

evidence_quotes.quote: En tanto, los servicios están descentralizados y constitucionalmente las provincias tienen el dominio originario de sus recursos naturales, no existe una Ley Nacional del Agua que fije lineamientos de la política hídrica ni una política unificada de los servicios de agua y saneamiento en todo el territorio.

En una primera aproximación se identificaron y relevaron los documentos y los datos de cobertura de los servicios de los Censos; luego se clasificó la información recogida, se delinearon las etapas de la política y se analizó la información.

En lo que concierne a la cobertura, mientras que en el 2001: el 77 % de la población accedía al agua y al 42,5 % en el caso de las cloacas, en el 2010 alcanzaba al 82,6 % y 48,8 % de la población respectivamente. La cobertura en cada una de las jurisdicciones era heterogénea como permiten observar las figuras 4 y 5.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines piped drinking-water and sewer service coverage across Argentina from 1869 to 2014.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording vs. narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: This paper passes the plain/broad wording of Criterion 2 because it discusses legal, constitutional, institutional, regulatory, and public/private management frameworks across five historical stages of Argentina's water and sanitation policy (decentralization, 1990s privatizations, regulatory agencies, and post-2002 re-statizations). However, it fails the narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type mechanism reading because it presents an unanalysed macro-governance historical background (1869–2014 periodization) rather than empirically analysing how utility ownership, regulatory structure, tariff rules, or disconnection rules directly govern service access.
criterion_notes.c3: Does not contain original empirical evidence or a systematic empirical synthesis on a governance-access mechanism. Explicit aim is to contribute to policy reflection and debate via a five-stage historical periodization based on narrative review of prior literature, institutional reports, laws, and descriptive aggregate INDEC census coverage trends (1910–2010); claims about impacts of privatization on access and affordability rely entirely on citing secondary literature. Excluded as E05.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports descriptive national and provincial percentages of population and households connected to piped water and sewer networks from INDEC censuses (1910–2010 and 2001 vs. 2010).
criterion_notes.c5: Lacks an identifiable analytical empirical study design and analytical exposure-outcome linkage: aggregate census coverage charts (Figures 1, 2, 4, 5) and a secondary catalog of provincial utilities (Tables 1–6) are presented descriptively alongside a 145-year narrative without linking variation in any legal, regulatory, or ownership exposure to coverage outcomes.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish with English title and abstract; per Inclusion Criterion 10, Spanish is directly readable and translatable from the provided full text for full methodological assessment, though the study is ineligible on E05/c2/c3/c5 grounds.

study_design: Narrative historical and policy overview with descriptive secondary census statistics
population_and_sample: National population and households across Argentina's 24 jurisdictions (published aggregate INDEC census figures, 1910–2010)
exposure: Macro-historical stages of national and provincial water and sanitation sector policy in Argentina (1869–2014: centralized state provision, decentralization, privatization, and re-statization; no specific analytical exposure evaluated)
outcome: Descriptive piped water network and sewer connection coverage (% of population and % of households from published INDEC censuses)
rationale: Excluded as E05 (No empirical evidence). Cáceres (2014) is a Spanish-language historical and policy overview aimed at contributing to debate and reflection on Argentina's water and sanitation sector through a five-stage periodization from 1869 to 2014. Although it reproduces aggregate national and provincial water and sewer coverage statistics from INDEC censuses and compiles a secondary table of provincial utilities and regulators, it contains no primary empirical data, no analytical empirical design linking any legal, regulatory, or ownership mechanism to service access outcomes, and is not a systematic empirical synthesis (relying on narrative citations of prior secondary studies for claims about privatization impacts). It also fails the narrow 2026-10-13 reading of Criterion 2 as unanalysed macro-governance background, and remains excluded under the plain Criterion 2 wording due to lack of empirical evaluation (c3/c5).
